createOrReplace.title: Low-Code vs Custom Development: 2026 Benchmarks
createOrReplace.html:
Low-code vs custom development is a choice about who builds your software and how much control you keep. Low-code platforms ship standard internal tools faster; custom development wins when the software is core, integration-heavy or must scale. App Builder's 2025 survey found 98% of tech leaders saved development time with low-code, but most of the hard limits show up later.

This matters now because the build side of build-vs-buy has become cheap and crowded. Retool's 2026 Build vs. Buy Report found 35% of teams have already replaced at least one SaaS tool with a custom build, and 78% expect to build more internal tools in 2026. In India, the low-code platform market alone was worth $399.3 million in 2022, according to Grand View Research. Indian operators are being pitched low-code, AI app builders and custom development in the same week. The numbers below show where each one actually fits.

TL;DR

  • 98% of tech leaders report development time savings with low-code, and 62% have cut development costs (App Builder, 2025).
  • Gartner forecast low-code tools would account for 75% of new application development by 2026, up from 40% in 2021.
  • 35% of teams have replaced a SaaS tool with a custom build; workflow automation is the top category at 35% (Retool, 2026).
  • 60% of builders shipped software outside IT oversight in the past year, and 25% do it frequently (Retool, 2026).
  • India's low-code platform market is projected to reach $2,896.8 million by 2030, growing at a 28.1% CAGR (Grand View Research).

What is the difference between low-code and custom development?

Low-code means building apps with a vendor's visual tools and pre-built components; custom development means writing your own code on infrastructure you control, with no platform ceiling.

In practice the line is blurrier than vendors suggest. Most low-code platforms let developers drop into code for edge cases, and most custom builds now use frameworks, open-source libraries and AI coding assistants that remove a lot of boilerplate. The real differences are three: who owns the runtime (the vendor or you), who can make changes (business users or engineers), and what happens when you hit something the platform was not designed for. For an Indian manufacturer, that might be a shop-floor app that has to talk to a 15-year-old Tally or SAP instance, a weighbridge and a WhatsApp gateway at once.

How widely are low-code platforms used in 2026?

Very widely: 95% of firms used low-code or no-code tools for software development in the last year, according to App Builder's survey reported by IT Pro.

That matches earlier research. IT Pro notes Forrester reported in 2024 that 88% of developers were using low-code platforms. Gartner's forecast, reported by InfoWorld, put the low-code development technologies market at $44.5 billion by 2026, growing 19% over four years, with low-code application platforms alone reaching nearly $10 billion in 2023 on 25% growth. Gartner also expected citizen developers to make up at least 80% of the low-code user base by 2026, up from 60% in 2021.

India is smaller but growing faster. Grand View Research estimates India accounted for 5.9% of the global low-code platform market in 2022, with web-based apps taking a 67.49% revenue share, and projects a 28.1% CAGR to 2030. Forecasts disagree a lot: a NASSCOM estimate reported by Analytics India Magazine put India's low-code/no-code market at about $400 million in FY2021, growing at 15% a year since 2019, and projected $4 billion to $4.2 billion by 2025. Treat market sizes as direction, not budget input.

Does low-code actually save time and money?

Yes, for the right kind of app: App Builder found 98% of tech leaders saved development time and 62% reduced development costs with low-code and no-code tools.

The size of the saving is the more useful number. According to the same survey of 300 US tech employees and managers, 78% saved up to 50% of development time, and 67% said they cut costs by up to 30%. Only 10% cut costs by more than half. So the typical win is real but bounded: a form-heavy approval workflow that would take an engineer weeks can ship in days, but you are not getting software for free. Licences, per-user fees and platform specialists replace some of the engineering cost rather than removing it.

Why are companies replacing SaaS tools with custom builds?

Because AI has made building cheaper, and off-the-shelf tools often do not fit: Retool found 35% of teams have already swapped at least one SaaS tool for a custom build.

Retool's report, based on 817 builders surveyed in late 2025, shows which tools are most exposed. Workflow automation tools lead at 35%, then internal admin tools at 33%, BI tools at 29%, CRMs and form builders at 25%, project management at 23% and customer support at 21%. These are exactly the categories where Indian SMBs pay per-seat fees for software they use a fraction of. Note the bias: this is a vendor survey of Retool's own users, so it reflects people who already build.

SaaS categoryShare replaced or at riskTypical low-code fit
Workflow automations35%Strong for approvals; weak for high-volume integrations
Internal admin tools33%Strong
BI tools29%Good for dashboards; data model still needs engineering
CRMs and form builders25%Good for forms; CRM depth favours custom or SaaS
Project management23%Moderate
Customer support21%Weak; channels and SLAs need custom work

Source: Retool 2026 Build vs. Buy Report (shares); fit column is Fine Solves' qualitative view.

What are the risks of low-code and citizen developers?

The main risks are ungoverned apps, security gaps and maintenance debt: Retool found 60% of builders shipped software outside IT oversight in the past year.

A quarter of them, 25%, do so frequently. Their reasons are practical: 31% say they can build faster than IT, 18% say IT processes are too slow, and 10% say official tools do not integrate.

The data on AI-assisted building is a warning too. Retool found only 8% of builders use AI-generated code without changes, while 44% test it thoroughly. When teams try to get automations into production, the top blockers are lack of engineering bandwidth at 42%, security and compliance at 41% and integration challenges at 39%, with maintenance burdens cited by 26%. In other words, the hard parts of software do not go away on a low-code canvas.

When should you choose custom development over low-code?

Choose custom development when the software is a differentiator, touches many systems, holds regulated data, or will serve customers at scale; choose low-code for internal, form-and-workflow apps with stable rules.

QuestionLeans low-codeLeans custom development
Who uses it?Internal staff, tens of usersCustomers, partners, or thousands of users
How many systems does it touch?One or two with standard connectorsERP, legacy databases, devices, government APIs
Is it a differentiator?No, it is plumbingYes, it is how you compete
Data sensitivityLow, internal operational dataHealth, financial or personal data under DPDP rules
Expected lifespanMonths to a couple of yearsFive years or more

Source: Fine Solves decision framework, informed by the Retool and App Builder survey data above.

Lock-in deserves its own line. A low-code app lives on the vendor's runtime and pricing. If per-user licences rise or the vendor changes direction, moving 40 apps off the platform is a rebuild, not a migration. Custom code you own can be moved, audited and extended by any competent team.

How do you decide: a 6-step playbook

  1. List the apps, not the platform. Write down the 10 to 20 tools your teams want, with users, systems touched and data type for each.
  2. Sort by the decision table above. Internal, low-risk, few integrations goes to low-code; core, regulated or customer-facing goes to custom development.
  3. Price the full lifecycle. Compare licences and per-user fees over five years against build plus maintenance, not just the first release.
  4. Test the hardest integration first. Before committing to a platform, build the one connection you fear most, such as your ERP or a legacy SQL database.
  5. Put guardrails on citizen developers. With 60% of builders already working outside IT oversight, give them a sanctioned platform, data access rules and a review step instead of a ban.
  6. Plan the exit. For every low-code app, note how you would export the data and logic if you had to rebuild it.

What this means for Indian businesses

For Indian mid-market firms the answer is usually both. Low-code platforms suit the long tail of internal tools: approvals, checklists, simple dashboards. Custom development suits the systems that run the business: production planning, dispatch, hospital billing, dealer portals and anything that has to integrate with GST, e-way bills, ABDM or a legacy ERP.

The survey data says low-code saves time on the first kind and that engineering bandwidth, security and integration remain the bottlenecks on the second. From the way we build at Fine Solves, the expensive mistakes come from putting a core system on a platform chosen for a simple one. If you are weighing low-code vs custom development for a specific system, Talk to Fine Solves.

Frequently asked questions

Is low-code cheaper than custom development?

Often, for simple internal apps. App Builder's 2025 survey found 62% of companies using low-code cut development costs, and 67% of tech leaders saw cuts of up to 30%. The saving shrinks for complex, integration-heavy systems, and recurring licence and per-user fees can outweigh the initial saving over several years.

Will AI replace low-code platforms?

Tech leaders do not expect it to. In App Builder's survey, 84% said AI will not replace their reliance on low-code and no-code tools, and 76% said AI will make existing tools more efficient. AI coding assistants are, however, making custom development faster, which narrows low-code's speed advantage.

What are citizen developers?

Citizen developers are business staff, not professional engineers, who build apps using low-code or no-code tools. Gartner forecast they would make up at least 80% of the low-code user base by 2026. They need guardrails: data access rules, a sanctioned platform and an IT review before apps go into production.

How big is the low-code market in India?

Grand View Research estimates India's low-code development platform market at $399.3 million in 2022 and projects $2,896.8 million by 2030, a 28.1% CAGR. Other estimates differ widely, so use these figures as a sign of direction rather than as an input to your own budget.

When is custom development the better choice?

Custom development is better when the software is core to how you compete, touches several systems such as ERP and legacy databases, handles regulated health or financial data, serves customers at scale, or needs to last five years or more without depending on a single vendor's runtime and pricing.
